newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money edges up to 9.5/10.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money edges up to 9.5/10.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged up to 9.5/10.0 percent after trading at 8.0/9.0 percent earlier on Tuesday on increased rupiah demand, dealers said.

One Japanese bank dealer said there was a slight tightening in mid-morning, probably due to weekly tax payments due Tuesday and also due to a moderate central bank supply of 210 billion rupiah into the market.

Another dealer said bidding from some small banks seemed to have also lifted rates. Longer-term rates were also soft on relatively ample short-term funds. One-week money was at 10.0/10.5, one-month at 12.5 and three-month at 13.50 percent.
The central bank lowered its two-week bilateral papers (SBIs) by 25 basis points while keeping others unchanged.
The central bank offered one-week SBIs at 6.5, two-week at 8.25 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent and three-month at 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 10.82 percent, compared with 11.5 percent on Friday.
Bond dealers said market focus was on upcoming new issues such as Bunas Finance and Ciputra Surya.
One dealer said overall prices were little changed in slow trading. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
